clue.text: Reward means death for an evildoer!

definitions.meaning: from Romans 6:23, 'the ... of sin is death'

explanation.definitionFit: Payment for labour is a reward, and the Bible says sin's payment is death, so both senses fit one word.

clue.text: A drop of Adam's ale?

parts.note: Adam's ale is a jocular name for water; 'a drop' is a fall of it rather than a small amount

explanation.surface: Just a little sip of plain water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A drop' suggests a tiny quantity but means a descent: water dropping over a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a place where a river drops over a ledge.

clue.text: Compass overturned by scholar in steamboat

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole is turned upside down, reading upwards
the scholar sits inside the steamboat

parts.note: a tug is a small powered boat
MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: A navigation compass flipped over by an academic on a paddle steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: MA goes into TUG to give TMAUG; 'overturned' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass in the sense of scope or range is the full sweep of something.

clue.text: Plant produces weapon in perfect condition

parts.note: a spear is a weapon
mint means in perfect condition, as new

explanation.surface: A garden plant yields a pristine spear.
explanation.definitionFit: A herb used for flavouring is a garden plant of the mint family.

clue.text: One with spikenard and a share in agriculture?

definitions.text: One with spikenard and a share in agriculture?

parts.words: One with spikenard and a share in agriculture?
parts.note: a farm worker who drives the plough has a 'share' (the ploughshare blade), and a wild flower called spikenard bears his name too

explanation.surface: Someone holds a fragrant herb and a stake in a farming business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Share' looks like a financial stake but is the cutting blade of a plough; ploughman's spikenard is a European wild plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm labourer who works a plough uses its share blade, and a plant called ploughman's spikenard carries the same name.

clue.text: Countryman training qua worker

parts.note: PE is physical education, training
qua means in the capacity of, i.e. as
a worker ant

explanation.surface: A farm lad trains in his role as labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural farm worker of humble rank is a man of the countryside.

clue.text: Surpass public military exercise

parts.note: overt means open, public
op, short for operation, a military exercise

explanation.surface: Outdo everyone in an open army manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise above or exceed something is to outdo it.

clue.text: Instrument: for a doctor in a southern state

indicators.note: the article and doctor are placed within the state's letters

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for Georgia, a US southern state
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A musical instrument wanted for a physician in the Deep South.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor and the article go inside the abbreviation for Georgia, splitting its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The viola da gamba is a bowed string viol, a musical instrument.

clue.text: Region of China with a rum representation

indicators.note: the letters are presented again in a new form

explanation.surface: A part of China portrayed with an odd image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' means strange in British slang, but here it is simply letters; CHINA plus A RUM are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchuria is a historical territory in north-east China.

clue.text: Fabric from a town in Ontario

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cloth produced in a small Canadian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a sheer lightweight silk or nylon dress material.

clue.text: Abstemious student leaves church with speed

indicators.note: the student departs from the place of worship, so his letter is taken out of it

parts.note: a temple is a place of worship
L is the learner-driver plate letter, standing for a student
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A sober scholar walks out of church at a brisk pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone moderate in food and drink is restrained, the sense of both words.

clue.text: The fellow supported by Prevost's heroine

parts.note: man means a fellow
'on' means resting upon, i.e. supported by

explanation.surface: A man is propped up by the heroine of a French novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Abbé Prévost wrote the 1731 novel Manon Lescaut, later an opera by Massenet and Puccini.
explanation.definitionFit: Manon Lescaut is the title character of the Abbé Prévost novel, its female lead.

clue.text: Revolutionary member engaged in distribution perhaps

definitions.text: Revolutionary member engaged in distribution perhaps

parts.words: Revolutionary member engaged in distribution perhaps
parts.note: a spinning part of a machine, such as the arm that turns inside a car engine's ignition distributor

explanation.surface: A rebel party member hands out leaflets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics but means turning round; the distributor is the car part that sends current to each spark plug.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating machine component turns round and round, as the arm in an ignition distributor does.

clue.text: An Eastern ruler accepting arts rejected in Russia

indicators.note: the ruler's title takes the other letters into itself

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, a form of 'an'
a khan is a ruler in Central Asia

indicators.note: the word arts is turned back, read from right to left

explanation.surface: An Asian potentate welcomes artists spurned in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Russia' is a terse definition: a place in Russia, the Volga city that gave its name to a curly lambskin.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is a city on the Volga delta, a place found within Russia.

clue.text: Prescribe a very soft semi-unguent

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

indicators.note: half of the word for an unguent is kept, its front part

parts.note: an unguent is an ointment

explanation.surface: A doctor orders a mild, half-strength cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-' keeps OINT, the front half of OINTMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint is to lay down or decree, the sense of prescribing a rule.

clue.text: Element identified by Kepler initially.

parts.note: the astronomer did not discover it; his name's first letter is this element's chemical symbol

explanation.surface: A chemical element discovered by Kepler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'identified' suggests discovery, but the element is merely labelled K, the initial of Kepler.
explanation.definitionFit: Its chemical symbol is K, from the Latin kalium, matching the astronomer's first letter.

clue.text: Christian's form of treatment sounds ghastly

indicators.note: the word for a form of treatment is said aloud, giving a shorter spelling

parts.note: a pill is a form of medical treatment
grim means ghastly

explanation.surface: A Christian's course of therapy seems horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: Christian is the hero of Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress; read 'Christian's' as 'Christian is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunyan's hero Christian makes a journey to the Celestial City, so he is a traveller on a religious journey.

clue.text: Fighter touching down about noon

indicators.note: the landing word goes round the letter for noon

parts.note: lighting means alighting, coming down to land

explanation.surface: A warplane lands at around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The English Electric Lightning was a British jet fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lightning was a supersonic RAF interceptor aircraft.

clue.text: Leo X, for one, raised Asian coin for drugs

parts.note: Pope Leo X was a member of the Medici family of Florence

indicators.note: in a down clue the coin's name is lifted, reading upwards

parts.note: sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries

explanation.surface: A Renaissance pope collected Eastern money to buy remedies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SEN into NES.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugs in the sense of remedies are medical preparations.

clue.text: Untruths about youngster are no small matter? Could be

indicators.note: the untruths go round the youngster

parts.note: lies are untruths
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Fibs told about a child are a serious business, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no small matter' is itself an example: a figure of speech that states something by denying its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Understatement by negation, as in calling a big thing 'no small matter', is that figure of speech.

clue.text: In bridge, the knack of being highly disciplined

indicators.note: the knack is put inside the bridge

parts.note: a span is a bridge
art means a knack or skill

explanation.surface: At the card table, discipline is a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game but is a span across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was famed for austere military training, so the adjective means strict and self-denying.

clue.text: Territory owned by W. E. Henley, do we assume? …

definitions.text: Territory owned by W. E. Henley, do we assume? …

parts.words: Territory owned by W. E. Henley, do we assume?
parts.note: the Victorian poet W. E. Henley wrote a patriotic poem whose refrain claims a country as 'my' own

explanation.surface: Whose land did the poet Henley possess?
explanation.walkthrough: Henley's poem 'Pro Rege Nostro' repeats the line 'England, my England', so the poet seems to claim the country as his property.
explanation.definitionFit: Henley's refrain addresses his homeland, the country of the English, as his own.

clue.text: Possibly the one state to be morally correct

indicators.note: the letters of the word may be arranged differently

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Perhaps the only nation that behaves rightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical conduct conforms to principles of right and wrong.

clue.text: … being a native of which, she scans a new composition

indicators.note: the letters are given a fresh arrangement, composed anew

explanation.surface: A woman from that land reads through a newly written poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 20 across: a native of that country. 'new composition' rearranges SHE SCANS A.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots use this word for an English person, someone born in the country of 20 across.

clue.text: Female is on the record to parishioners

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: she is a female pronoun
EP, extended play, is a record

explanation.surface: A woman gives her statement to the people of the parish.
explanation.walkthrough: A congregation is the pastor's flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchgoers are the flock tended by their pastor, so they are figuratively his woolly animals.

clue.text: Provide stimulus like a click beetle?

definitions.meaning: a click beetle is called an ..., so jokingly it must do what its name says

explanation.definitionFit: To excite or buoy up someone is to stimulate them, and the beetle's Latin name elater means one who does just that.

clue.text: Do put a heavyweight in charge

parts.note: a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: Appoint a big hitter to lead.
explanation.walkthrough: In tonic sol-fa the note Do (doh) is the keynote of the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Doh is the first note of the sol-fa scale, the keynote of the key.

clue.text: Sound from one in the middle of organ recital

indicators.note: one goes into the centre of the organ

parts.note: the nose is an organ of the body
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Music comes out of a church organ performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests music but is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud din or racket is unwanted sound.

clue.text: Little by little a shrub takes shape

parts.note: Eric, or Little by Little is F. W. Farrar's 1858 school story, so its title character stands for the subtitle

explanation.surface: Gradually, a bush grows into form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little by little' looks like an adverb but is the subtitle of a Victorian schoolboy novel whose hero is Eric.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical name of heath and heather, low evergreen bushes.

clue.text: Change course with artist, say — a skilful mover

indicators.note: the two words are spoken together to give a near match

parts.note: to tack is to change course when sailing; Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: Switch direction with a painter, a deft operator.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategist plans clever moves, in chess or war, so is a skilful mover of pieces.

clue.text: Blooming Blakeney!

parts.note: Sir Percy Blakeney is the hero of Baroness Orczy's novels, known by the name of a scarlet wild flower; 'blooming' makes him a flower

explanation.surface: An exasperated oath at someone called Blakeney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' reads as a mild British curse but means flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: Blakeney's alias, the Scarlet ___, is a small red-flowered plant.

clue.text: Mounts for the 2nd Dragoons?

parts.note: the 2nd Dragoons were the Royal Scots cavalry regiment nicknamed after the colour of their horses

explanation.surface: Which horses would a cavalry regiment ride?
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Scots Greys, a British cavalry regiment, rode grey horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The regiment's nickname came from its pale-coated horses, so these horses suit it.
